adrManager.adrDirectory.description: Path to the ADR directory, relative to the workspace root.

adrManager.adrNamespace.description: Override the project namespace for cross-project ADR citations (e.g., 'my-project'). Auto-detected from git remote if empty.

adrManager.newAdrTargetRoot.description: Which root a new ADR/Seed is created in, in a multi-root workspace (ADR-0025 Decision 6). 'active-editor' (default) follows whichever root your current file lives in, prompting only when that can't be determined. Set to a specific root's namespace (hover a root in the sidebar to see it) to pin that root regardless of which file is active — useful when focused on one subproject for a sprint.

adrManager.alwaysPromptOnMultiRoot.description: Always show a picker for which root to create a new ADR/Seed in, even when adrManager.newAdrTargetRoot would otherwise resolve one silently.

enumDescriptions: Always "owner/repo", from each root's git origin remote.
Always just the repo name, from each root's git origin remote.
Repo name alone when all (or most) roots share one owner; owner/repo only for the roots whose owner isn't the majority.
adrManager.roots.captionMode.description: How each root's caption is shown in a multi-root tree. Falls back to adrManager.adrNamespace / the auto-detected project namespace for a root with no discoverable git remote.

adrManager.humanName.description: Your name as the human collaborator. Pre-fills the 'Deciders' field in new ADRs and the 'Answering as:' field in the Open Questions panel. Falls back to git config user.name if empty.

adrManager.showAuthorshipField.description: Show the 'Answering as:' name field in the Open Questions panel. Off by default — the capability is unchanged (adrManager.humanName / git config still supply the author name either way); this only controls whether the field itself takes up space in the dialog.

adrManager.aiModel.description: The AI model name used in new ADR templates — set this once to whatever you're actually using (e.g., 'Sonnet 5', 'Claude Opus 5'). Left as an obvious placeholder by default rather than a specific model name, since that name is guaranteed to go stale.

adrManager.logging.panelErrors.description: When an error occurs in the Open Questions panel, append a full-reconstruction record (entire ADR text, entire answer box, all metadata) to the owning project's docs/adr/.working/errors.jsonl. Default OFF as of the first public release (ship-flip, docs/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md) — was ON during pre-launch error collection; a stranger's working directory shouldn't quietly fill with our telemetry the moment they hit an error. Turn on locally if you want the diagnostic detail.

adrManager.logging.tourUnresolvedRefs.description: When a tour is opened/refreshed with an unresolvable reference, append a full-reconstruction record (the tour's own JSON, every unresolved ref with its reason, and every real file the tour touched) to the project's error ledger. Default OFF as of the first public release (ship-flip, docs/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md) — was ON during pre-launch error collection.

adrManager.logging.observations.description: Whether the Report button (adrManager.reportButton.enabled) actually writes to the error ledger. Default OFF as of the first public release (ship-flip, docs/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md) — was ON during pre-launch error collection. Turning this on keeps the button visible and enables the write, e.g. if you want to help us diagnose something.

adrManager.renderMarkdownInQuestionTitle.description: Render inline Markdown (`code`, **bold**, _italic_) in question titles in the Open Questions panel. Titles in the sidebar tree always show plain text (backticks stripped).

enumDescriptions: Scroll to the ### QST: heading (shows the full question context)
Scroll to the **ANS:** field (jump straight to where you type)
adrManager.clickNavigatesTo.description: When clicking a question in the tree or navigating from the panel, where to scroll in the file.

enumDescriptions: Click a question in the sidebar to open it in the Open Questions panel, focused and ready to answer.
Click a question in the sidebar to jump straight to it in the ADR/seed file.
adrManager.clickOpensIn.description: Where clicking a question in the sidebar tree takes you. The panel is answerable in place; file access stays one right-click away either way ("Go to Answer Field in File").

enumDescriptions: A vscode://.../open link naming a question opens the Open Questions panel, navigated to it; a link naming just an ADR/seed (no question) reveals it in the tree instead.
Always reveal and focus the target in the ADR Explorer tree, including the specific question when the link names one.
Always open the plain markdown file at the target's line — the off-switch, same as before this handler existed.
adrManager.deepLink.openIn.description: Where opening a vscode://jlumbroso.adrs4ai/open?target=<adr://...> link (e.g. from Pigeonhole) lands. Falls back to the markdown file whenever the preferred surface can't show the target (hidden by a tree filter, or the link doesn't resolve at all) — never silently does nothing.

enumDescriptions: Preview the 3 lines before/after where a fresh ANS block would be inserted, with a confirm step, before writing.
Insert the fresh ANS block immediately, no preview (fast, but the insertion point is a computed guess, not an exact marker match).
Never insert a fresh ANS block automatically — always ask you to answer that question manually in the file.
adrManager.missingAnsBehavior.description: What to do when a question has a recognized Status field but no **ANS:** marker or [Fill this in] placeholder at all — the panel has to append a fresh ANS block rather than fill an exact spot. DEBRIEF-006 (2026-07-18): this insertion point is a computed guess, not an exact match, and a mis-scanned block boundary once spliced an answer into the middle of someone else's recommendation. Default "confirm" shows you the surrounding lines before committing.

adrManager.badge.include.adr.description: ADR-0029: include ADR questions in the sidebar badge's open-question count. Defaulting all sources on gives an implicit "badge off" when every source is disabled — no separate master toggle.

adrManager.badge.include.seed.description: ADR-0029: include seed questions in the sidebar badge's open-question count.

adrManager.badge.showParseHealth.description: ADR-0029 (fold addendum, 2026-07-12): the sidebar badge's tooltip discloses parse health alongside the open-question count — "N open questions · M files with parse warnings" — so a confident number can't silently license inattention. The tooltip only appears on hover (pull, not push), so this is on by default; turn it off if you'd rather have models attend to parse warnings exclusively.

adrManager.mcpWriteMode.description: How MCP write operations modify ADR files. 'workspaceEdit' uses VS Code's undo-safe edit API; 'direct' writes directly to disk.

enumDescriptions: Before committing, show a pre-checked checklist of untracked files mentioned in what you're about to commit (a screenshot linked from a seed/ADR is the motivating case) — confirm which to include.
Silently include every mentioned untracked file, no prompt.
Never include mentioned untracked files automatically — commit them yourself when you want to.
adrManager.commit.untrackedReferences.description: ADR Commit: what to do about untracked files mentioned in the content you're about to commit. Only checked in the single-root interactive commit — the multi-root batch commit never prompts, to keep 'select all, go' actually one gesture (auto-commit still applies there; ask behaves as auto-ignore).

adrManager.commitOnAnswerSubmit.description: When you submit an answer in the Open Questions panel, immediately git-commit that one file (pathspec'd, so it can never sweep up unrelated work). Founder-commissioned protection (Concertmaster 5 forensics, 2026-10-11): a crew git operation with no uncommitted-changes guard (e.g. `git checkout <tree-ish> -- <path>`) can silently overwrite a just-submitted answer before anyone commits it — this shrinks that window to the time between the save and the commit. Off by default: an extension committing on your behalf, even to one file, is a real behavior change not every workflow wants.

adrManager.panel.bodyMaxWidth.description: Max width of the Open Questions panel body. A pixel value (e.g. '1100') is combined with a 94% viewport cap so it never overflows a narrow window; 'full' removes the cap entirely (fit the whole question in your window).

adrManager.panel.recommendationCollapseT.description: When a question has stacked recommendations (ADR-0019), collapse all but the most recent N behind an "N earlier recommendation(s)" disclosure. 0 (default) never collapses — every recommendation stays expanded, like an LLM harness's thinking traces.

enumDescriptions: Never show which root a question belongs to.
Show it only when the current question set spans more than one root.
Always show it, even in a single-root workspace.
adrManager.panel.showProjectInHeader.description: Show the owning root's caption flush-right next to "Question N of M" in the Open Questions panel — helps when paging through questions from several projects at once (adrManager.roots.captionMode controls the exact text shown).

adrManager.sidebar.categoryOrder.description: Order of the Tours/ADRs/Seeds categories in the sidebar tree. A category with nothing in it (e.g. no tours minted yet) is still omitted entirely, same as before — this only controls the order of whichever categories are actually showing.

adrManager.seeds.agingMode.description: How the sidebar decides a seed's staleness dimming threshold (ADR-0041). 'adaptive' (default): the threshold scales with this repo's own rhythm (adrManager.seeds.adaptiveMultiplier × the repo's median days-since-last-activity among actively-iterating seeds) — a 25-day idle seed in a house whose normal pulse is a 27-day median isn't unusual. 'fixed': always adrManager.seeds.fixedThresholdDays, regardless of repo rhythm.

adrManager.seeds.adaptiveMultiplier.description: Multiplier applied to the repo's median seed-activity age when adrManager.seeds.agingMode is 'adaptive' (ADR-0041's ratified default: 0.5 — e.g. a 27-day median dims at ~14 days). Ignored in 'fixed' mode.

adrManager.seeds.fixedThresholdDays.description: Days of inactivity before a seed dims, when adrManager.seeds.agingMode is 'fixed'. Also the fallback used in 'adaptive' mode when there's no measurable repo-wide activity to adapt to (e.g. an empty or brand-new seed set).

adrManager.seeds.showOpenQuestionCount.description: Show a seed's open-question count (e.g. '· 3 open') in the sidebar description, alongside its lifecycle state (ADR-0041). This is content-state, not lifecycle — turn off if you'd rather the description show only lifecycle/rollup.

adrManager.tours.showLeanVerbPrefix.description: In a tour's treeview entries, prefix each question with its authored disposition — DECIDE / RATIFY / ACKNOWLEDGE / DELEGATE — when the tour sets one. An entry with no disposition set gets no prefix.

adrManager.tours.hideCompleted.description: Hide fully-done tours from the sidebar's Tours category. Toggle from the Tours category's own right-click menu (Hide/Show Completed Tours) or here.

adrManager.adrs.hideSettled.description: Hide ADRs whose status is Implemented, Superseded, or paused (Deferred/Paused/Suspended/On Hold) from the sidebar's ADRs category — the decisions that aren't actively being worked. Toggle from the ADRs category's own right-click menu (Hide/Show Settled ADRs) or here.

adrManager.adrs.hideWithoutOpenQuestions.description: Hide ADRs with no open questions from the sidebar's ADRs category. Toggle from the ADRs category's own right-click menu (Hide/Show ADRs Without Open Questions), a project root's right-click menu (Hide/Show Without Open Questions, together with the Seeds equivalent), or here.

adrManager.seeds.hideClosed.description: Hide closed-family seeds (parked/superseded/terminated) from the sidebar's Seeds category. Toggle from the Seeds category's own right-click menu (Hide/Show Closed Seeds) or here.

adrManager.seeds.hideWithoutOpenQuestion.description: Hide seeds with no open questions from the sidebar's Seeds category. Toggle from the Seeds category's own right-click menu (Hide/Show Seeds Without Open Questions), a project root's right-click menu (Hide/Show Without Open Questions, together with the ADRs equivalent), or here.

adrManager.reportButton.enabled.description: Show a 'Report' button in the Open Questions panel — captures the current ADR's full content, a note you type, and basic panel state to the project's error ledger (docs/adr/.working/errors.jsonl), without touching your in-progress answer. Off by default; turn on if you want a frictionless way to flag a problem without leaving the panel.

adrManager.unresolved.hideFromPanel.description: ADR-0036: hide 'Status: unresolved' questions (the ball is in the model's court) from the Open Questions panel — the human-facing answer queue. Off by default: an unresolved question still shows there today, and stays that way unless you turn this on.

adrManager.deferred.hideFromPanel.description: ADR-0036: hide 'Status: deferred' questions (blocked on data/build/users — nobody's ball right now) from the Open Questions panel. Off by default, same reasoning as adrManager.unresolved.hideFromPanel.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No decision records yet — this project's deliberation starts here.
[Start your first decision record](command:adrManager.createAdr)
Or begin from the [companion template](https://github.com/ADRs4AI/human-ai-collaboration-template-A) — starter files that give an AI model the vocabulary this extension expects.
Your thinking stops disappearing. Your decisions start compounding.

walkthroughs.description: From first decision record to an AI answering through the record — four steps.

Every unanswered question, one sidebar, answered in place.
